# Day-ahead model (issue 10:00 on D-1): analysis, test period (generated by `scripts/analyze_dayahead.py`; plan task 9.7)

Design: `docs/experiment_protocol.md`, entry of 2026-10-19. Predictions of `scripts/run_dayahead.py` (frozen configuration, single test evaluation). 8,611 (day, hour) samples; 355 days with all 24 valid hours. Naive = the better of the two naive baselines on validation (same hour on the latest earlier day). Intervals: 95% paired moving-block bootstrap over whole days (blocks of 28 days, 1,000 resamples, fixed seed).

## Cost of issuing once per day: day-ahead versus the rolling 24 h-ahead forecasts

Same target hours (8,611 hours; 355 complete days in both sets). The rolling forecasts are the 24 h-ahead forecasts of the frozen main run (`h24.npz`), each issued 24 h before its target hour with the latest data at that time; the day-ahead forecasts are issued once at 10:00 on the previous day. The two sets of models use different leads, features and tuning, so this is a descriptive comparison, not a controlled experiment. Difference = day-ahead minus rolling (positive = the fixed issue time costs accuracy).

| model | hourly MAE day-ahead (MW) | hourly MAE rolling 24 h (MW) | difference (95% CI) | energy MAE day-ahead (MU) | energy MAE rolling (MU) | difference (95% CI) | peak MAE day-ahead (MW) | peak MAE rolling (MW) | difference (95% CI) |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| Best naive | 6,224 | 5,414 | +811 (+614 to +1,041) | 128.6 | 101.2 | +27.4 (+21.1 to +33.3) | 5,586 | 5,086 | +500 (+17 to +911) |
| Ridge | 4,826 | 4,214 | +612 (+16 to +1,371) | 98.8 | 71.1 | +27.7 (+12.7 to +49.0) | 4,716 | 3,750 | +966 (+452 to +1,733) |
| XGBoost S4 | 4,120 | 3,728 | +391 (+239 to +476) | 82.5 | 68.9 | +13.6 (+9.9 to +16.1) | 4,001 | 3,420 | +581 (+177 to +910) |
| LSTM L4 | 4,634 | 3,743 | +891 (+675 to +1,243) | 94.0 | 67.0 | +27.0 (+20.1 to +35.4) | 4,734 | 3,416 | +1,318 (+838 to +1,960) |

Differences whose interval includes zero are not distinguishable.

## Caveats

- 355 complete days from one test year. Intervals reflect day-to-day sampling noise inside that period, not year-to-year variation.
- Scenario A: no forecast weather, so the day-ahead problem is harder than in practice where weather forecasts exist; forecast temperature helped at 24-72 h in the main study.
- The origin is the demand value of the hour starting at 10:00; the issue time and the availability of that value are assumptions of the design.
- XGBoost and the LSTM are pooled over the 24 target hours (one model each), ridge has one model per target hour; the per-hour XGBoost and a 24-output LSTM were not run.
- The test year has been used several times for declared analyses; this is a further use, with the design fixed beforehand.
